Authors: Silver, Edward A.; Pyke, David F.; Peterson, Rein
Title: Inventory Management and Production Planning and Scheduling (3rd ed.)
Forecasting_Methods: Lead-time demand convolutions; exponential smoothing; moving averages
Evaluation_Metrics: Fill rate (beta); cycle service level; holding and setup costs
Key_Empirical_Findings: Establishes canonical continuous-review (s, Q) replenishment dynamics and proves that safety stock buffer sizing is governed by the convolution of forecast error variance and lead-time variance.
Relevance_to_Our_Study: Provides the foundational inventory control equations, dynamic safety stock sizing, reorder point mechanics, and EOQ derivations implemented in src/inventory.py.

Authors: Croston, J. D.
Title: Forecasting and Stock Control for Intermittent Demands
Forecasting_Methods: Croston method separating demand size from inter-arrival intervals
Evaluation_Metrics: Forecast error variance; replenishment cycle stock
Key_Empirical_Findings: Demonstrates that standard exponential smoothing produces severe positive bias immediately following demand periods; decomposing demand into inter-arrival timing and non-zero transaction magnitudes stabilizes variance.
Relevance_to_Our_Study: Establishes the classical benchmark paradigm for intermittent demand and provides the analytical baseline for evaluating our zero-inflated M5 grocery series.

Authors: Syntetos, Aris A.; Boylan, John E.
Title: On the bias of intermittent demand estimates
Forecasting_Methods: Croston method; Simple Exponential Smoothing
Evaluation_Metrics: Mathematical expected bias; Mean Squared Error
Key_Empirical_Findings: Proves mathematically that Croston's estimator is positively biased by an exact factor of 1 / (1 - alpha/2), demonstrating that standard smoothing parameters induce systematic over-stocking.
Relevance_to_Our_Study: Directly informs our operational bias accounting, proving why percentage bias cannot be ignored when evaluating intermittent series.

Authors: Syntetos, Aris A.; Boylan, John E.
Title: The accuracy of intermittent demand estimates
Forecasting_Methods: Croston method; Syntetos-Boylan Approximation (SBA)
Evaluation_Metrics: Relative Absolute Error (RAE); Mean Squared Error (MSE); Percentage Bias
Key_Empirical_Findings: Formulates the SBA correction factor (1 - alpha/2) that deflates Croston's positive bias, resulting in strictly superior forecasting accuracy and inventory holding reductions across 3,000 automotive SKUs.
Relevance_to_Our_Study: Directly influences our operational safeguard constraints and illustrates the critical interaction between bias elimination and stock holding efficiency.

Authors: Boylan, John E.; Syntetos, Aris A.
Title: The accuracy of a Modified Croston procedure
Forecasting_Methods: Modified Croston; SBA; Original Croston
Evaluation_Metrics: Mean Absolute Scaled Error; Bias; Holding vs Shortage Cost
Key_Empirical_Findings: Demonstrates empirically that positive forecast bias severely inflates inventory holding capital while negative bias causes severe stockouts; categorizing demand prevents inappropriate model application.
Relevance_to_Our_Study: Validates our multi-regime categorization (Smooth Walmart, Lumpy Online Retail, Intermittent M5) and operational bias safeguard thresholds.

Authors: Willemain, Thomas R.; Smart, Charles N.; Schwarz, Henry F.
Title: A new approach to forecasting intermittent demand for service parts inventories
Forecasting_Methods: Markov bootstrap; Croston; Exponential Smoothing
Evaluation_Metrics: Cumulative LTD Distribution; Service Level Achieved; Inventory Value
Key_Empirical_Findings: Shows that non-parametric bootstrapping captures complex autocorrelation and autocorrelation in intermittent demand distributions far better than parametric Croston methods, reducing stockouts by up to 20%.
Relevance_to_Our_Study: Highlights the fundamental limitation of Gaussian distribution assumptions for intermittent lead-time demand, motivating our discrete event simulation.

Authors: Snyder, Ralph D.; Ord, J. Keith; Koehler, Anne B.
Title: Exponential smoothing models: Means and variances for lead-time demand
Forecasting_Methods: Single-source of error (SSOE) state-space models; ARIMA
Evaluation_Metrics: Lead-time demand mean and variance; Cycle Service Level
Key_Empirical_Findings: Derives exact analytical expressions for lead-time demand mean and variance under autocorrelated demand, proving that ignoring autocorrelation in lead times causes severe safety stock under-sizing.
Relevance_to_Our_Study: Provides the theoretical underpinning for compounding forecast residual error over lead times in src/inventory.py.

Authors: Hyndman, Rob J.; Koehler, Anne B.
Title: Another look at measures of forecast accuracy
Forecasting_Methods: MASE; MAPE; sMAPE; RMSE; MAE
Inventory_Setting: Empirical evaluation across M3 and intermittent panels
Evaluation_Metrics: Mean Absolute Scaled Error (MASE); Scale-independent loss
Key_Empirical_Findings: Demonstrates that MAPE is statistically invalid on intermittent demand due to division by zero and extreme right-tail skewness; establishes MASE and WAPE as stable scale-independent alternatives.
Relevance_to_Our_Study: Motivates the strict metric integrity rules in src/metrics.py, specifically zero-denominator safeguards and replacing raw MAPE with WAPE.

Authors: Wallström, Peter; Segerstedt, Anders
Title: Evaluation of forecasting error measurements and techniques for intermittent demand
Forecasting_Methods: Croston; SBA; Simple Moving Average; Linear Regression
Evaluation_Metrics: Number of periods in stock (PIS); Cumulative Forecast Error (CFE); WAPE
Key_Empirical_Findings: Proves that standard symmetric point metrics fail to capture the cumulative directional drift that ruins inventory replenishment; cumulative forecast error (bias) is the dominant driver of inventory health.
Relevance_to_Our_Study: Directly justifies our tri-criterion evaluation where signed percentage bias acts as a strict operational safeguard filter (Policy C).

Authors: Babai, M. Zied; Syntetos, Aris A.; Teunter, Ruud H.
Title: Determining order-up-to levels under periodic review for compound binomial (intermittent) demand
Forecasting_Methods: Compound binomial approximations; SBA; Croston
Evaluation_Metrics: Holding cost; backorder penalty; achieved fill rate
Key_Empirical_Findings: Establishes that selecting forecasting methods based strictly on minimum Mean Squared Error leads to sub-optimal order-up-to levels and inflated replenishment costs under intermittent orders.
Relevance_to_Our_Study: Foundational evidence for the decoupling between statistical error metrics and downstream inventory costs.

Authors: Teunter, Ruud H.; Syntetos, Aris A.; Babai, M. Zied
Title: Intermittent demand: Linking forecasting to inventory obsolescence
Forecasting_Methods: TSB method updating demand probability every period; Croston; SBA
Evaluation_Metrics: Mean Absolute Error; Bias; Obsolescent Inventory Cost
Key_Empirical_Findings: Proves that Croston and SBA fail to detect product obsolescence because probabilities update only on transaction days; period-by-period probability updating prevents holding dead inventory.
Relevance_to_Our_Study: Directly relevant to the M5 zero-inflated grocery dataset, where long runs of zero demand risk severe model drift and buffer over-sizing.

Authors: Eppen, Gary D.; Martin, R. Kipp
Title: Determining Safety Stock in the Presence of Stochastic Lead Time and Demand
Forecasting_Methods: Joint bivariate convolution of lead time and demand distributions
Evaluation_Metrics: Expected backorders; holding cost; cycle service level
Key_Empirical_Findings: Formulates the exact variance of lead-time demand under joint demand and lead-time stochasticity: Var(LTD) = E[L]*Var(D) + (E[D])^2*Var(L), proving lead-time variance often dominates demand variance.
Relevance_to_Our_Study: Direct mathematical specification for calculate_safety_stock with non-zero sigma_lead_time in src/inventory.py.

Authors: Trigg, D. W.
Title: Monitoring a Forecasting System
Forecasting_Methods: Exponentially smoothed error tracking; Mean Absolute Deviation (MAD)
Evaluation_Metrics: Tracking Signal TS = E_t / MAD_t
Key_Empirical_Findings: Proves that smoothing the ratio of cumulative smoothed forecast error to mean absolute deviation bounds tracking signals between [-1, 1], enabling automatic detection of out-of-control bias.
Relevance_to_Our_Study: Formulates the automated Trigg Tracking Signal surveillance deployed in Tier 4 and Algorithm 1 of our inventory decision support system.

Authors: Syntetos, Aris A.; Boylan, John E.; Disney, Stephen M.
Title: Forecasting for inventory planning: a 50-year review
Venue: Journal of the Operational Research Society
Forecasting_Methods: Exponential smoothing; Croston; state-space models; neural networks
Evaluation_Metrics: Forecast accuracy vs stock control costs; Bullwhip Effect
Key_Empirical_Findings: Comprehensive 50-year review identifying that the forecasting and inventory control disciplines evolved in isolation, leading to models that optimize irrelevant statistical surrogates.
Relevance_to_Our_Study: Provides historical and theoretical justification for bridging supervised machine learning directly with stochastic replenishment policies.

Authors: Kolassa, Stephan
Title: Evaluating predictive count data distributions in retail sales forecasting
Forecasting_Methods: Quantile regression; pinball loss; Poisson and Negative Binomial count models
Evaluation_Metrics: Pinball Loss; MAE; MSE; Service Level Shortage Cost
Key_Empirical_Findings: Proves that symmetric loss metrics (MSE, MAE) fail to align with retail economics where stockout costs typically exceed holding costs; pinball loss directly optimizes inventory quantile targets.
Relevance_to_Our_Study: Provides the theoretical foundation for asymmetric loss functions and pinball loss metrics in our metric integrity engine.

Authors: Syntetos, Aris A.; Babai, M. Zied; Boylan, John E.; Kolassa, Stephan; Nikolopoulos, Konstantinos
Title: Supply chain forecasting: Theory, practice, their gap and the future
Forecasting_Methods: Classical statistical; judgmental; supervised machine learning
Evaluation_Metrics: Forecast Value Added (FVA); MAPE; Carrying Cost; Stockout Penalty
Key_Empirical_Findings: Demonstrates that top-performing statistical accuracy models often fail to translate to reduced operational costs when lead-time variances, operational constraints, and stockout penalties are omitted.
Relevance_to_Our_Study: Establishes the research gap between predictive loss minimization and supply chain economic objectives addressed in our study.

Authors: Kourentzes, Nikolaos
Title: Intermittent demand forecasts with neural networks
Forecasting_Methods: Multilayer Perceptrons; Croston; SBA
Evaluation_Metrics: MAE; Percentage Bias; Inventory Holding & Shortage Cost
Key_Empirical_Findings: Shows that neural networks can identify non-linear arrival patterns, but if unconstrained by bias penalties, produce persistent under-forecasting bias that severely degrades customer service levels.
Relevance_to_Our_Study: Demonstrates that non-linear machine learning architectures without operational bias safeguards induce inventory starvation.

Authors: Kourentzes, Nikolaos; Petropoulos, Fotios; Assimakopoulos, Vassilios
Title: Improving forecasting by estimating time series structural components across multiple frequencies
Forecasting_Methods: MAPA; exponential smoothing; temporal ensembling
Evaluation_Metrics: MAPS; MAE; RMSE; Percentage Bias
Key_Empirical_Findings: Proves that estimating structural components across multiple temporal aggregation levels attenuates high-frequency noise and stabilizes forecasting performance without model misspecification.
Relevance_to_Our_Study: Provides theoretical support for cross-temporal aggregation and multi-scale feature engineering across weekly and daily retail panels.

Authors: Petropoulos, Fotios; Kourentzes, Nikolaos
Title: Forecast combinations for intermittent demand
Venue: Journal of the Operational Research Society
Forecasting_Methods: Intermittent Demand Combinations; SBA; Croston; SES
Evaluation_Metrics: Periods-In-Stock (PIS); MAE; PIS Holding Cost
Key_Empirical_Findings: Demonstrates that combining forecasts across multiple non-overlapping temporal aggregation levels dramatically reduces intermittent forecast variance and improves inventory holding efficiency.
Relevance_to_Our_Study: Supports ensembling strategies and multi-regime cross-sectional validation across diverse SKU velocity bands.

Authors: Breiman, Leo
Title: Random Forests
Forecasting_Methods: Random Forest Regressor
Evaluation_Metrics: Generalization error; Out-of-Bag (OOB) variance; Feature importance
Key_Empirical_Findings: Proves that aggregating randomized decorrelated decision trees achieves extreme variance reduction without increasing bias, demonstrating extreme robustness to noisy, skewed real-world data.
Relevance_to_Our_Study: Forms the theoretical basis for our Random Forest model, which demonstrates remarkable empirical resistance to the negative bias seen in gradient boosting.

Authors: Chen, Tianqi; Guestrin, Carlos
Title: XGBoost: A Scalable Tree Boosting System
Venue: Proceedings of the 22nd ACM SIGKDD International Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining
Forecasting_Methods: XGBoost (exact second-order Taylor expansion; sparsity-aware split)
Evaluation_Metrics: Squared Error; Logistic Loss; Training Wall-Clock Time
Key_Empirical_Findings: Formulates second-order gradient boosted trees with shrinkage and column subsampling, establishing formal optimization of custom loss landscapes and handling extreme sparsity.
Relevance_to_Our_Study: Algorithmic foundation for XGBoost models in our pipeline across Walmart, Online Retail, and M5.

Authors: Ke, Guolin; Meng, Qi; Finley, Thomas; Wang, Taifeng; Chen, Wei; Ma, Weidong; Ye, Qiwei; Liu, Tie-Yan
Title: LightGBM: A Highly Efficient Gradient Boosting Decision Tree
Venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 30 (NeurIPS 2017)
Forecasting_Methods: LightGBM (Gradient-based One-Side Sampling; Exclusive Feature Bundling)
Evaluation_Metrics: Training runtime; memory consumption; RMSE; WAPE
Key_Empirical_Findings: Introduces GOSS and EFB, enabling histogram-based gradient boosting that achieves up to 20x faster training while matching or exceeding conventional GBDT predictive accuracy.
Relevance_to_Our_Study: Primary high-efficiency model engine used for our multi-regime retail forecasting benchmark.

Authors: Böse, Jan-Hendrik; Flunkert, Valentin; Gasthaus, Jan; Januschowski, Tim; Lange, Dustin; Salinas, David; Scheifele, Clemens; Seung, Sebastian; Seeger, Michael W.
Title: Probabilistic demand forecasting at scale
Forecasting_Methods: Quantile Random Forests; Probabilistic Neural Networks; GBDT
Evaluation_Metrics: Quantile Loss; Under-replenishment Rate; Inventory Turnover
Key_Empirical_Findings: Demonstrates across Amazon fulfillment systems that direct optimization of quantile-specific asymmetric loss functions matching inventory service levels yields significantly lower end-to-end supply chain operational costs.
Relevance_to_Our_Study: Empirically validates our Policy D (Cost-Aware Selection) over standard unconstrained point accuracy (Policy B).

Authors: Salinas, David; Flunkert, Valentin; Gasthaus, Jan; Januschowski, Tim
Title: DeepAR: Probabilistic forecasting with autoregressive recurrent networks
Forecasting_Methods: DeepAR (LSTM autoregression with Negative Binomial / Gaussian likelihoods)
Evaluation_Metrics: Quantile Loss (rho_0.5, rho_0.9); RMSE; WAPE
Key_Empirical_Findings: Demonstrates that autoregressive probabilistic deep learning models generate calibrated predictive quantiles directly suitable for safety stock sizing, outperforming standard Gaussian point-forecast heuristics.
Relevance_to_Our_Study: Provides the probabilistic forecasting benchmark against which gradient boosted trees and residual standard error safety stocks are evaluated.

Authors: Lim, Bryan; Arık, Sercan Ö.; Loeff, Nicolas; Pfister, Tomas
Title: Temporal Fusion Transformers for interpretable multi-horizon time series forecasting
Forecasting_Methods: Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT); DeepAR; Seq2Seq; LightGBM
Evaluation_Metrics: Quantile Loss (P10, P50, P90); Attention Interpretability Weights
Key_Empirical_Findings: Proves that multi-horizon self-attention architectures capture complex heterogeneity across static and time-varying features while outputting prediction intervals directly usable for inventory buffers.
Relevance_to_Our_Study: Establishes state-of-the-art transformer baselines for multi-horizon enterprise forecasting.

Authors: Spiliotis, Evangelos; Abolghasemi, Mahdi; Hyndman, Rob J.; Petropoulos, Fotios; Assimakopoulos, Vassilios
Title: Cross-temporal aggregation: Improving the forecast accuracy of hierarchical electricity consumption
Forecasting_Methods: Cross-temporal hierarchical reconciliation; ML ensembles; ARIMA
Evaluation_Metrics: MASE; RMSSE; Percentage Bias
Key_Empirical_Findings: Demonstrates that reconciling high-frequency noise and intermittency with low-frequency trend signals across time horizons significantly reduces forecast volatility and stabilizes replenishment schedules.
Relevance_to_Our_Study: Provides the theoretical context for evaluating demand across different temporal resolutions (weekly Walmart vs daily Online Retail/M5).

Authors: Januschowski, Tim; Gasthaus, Jan; Wang, Yuyang; Salinas, David; Flunkert, Valentin; Bohlke-Schneider, Michael; Callot, Laurent
Title: Criteria for classifying forecasting methods
Forecasting_Methods: Cloud-scale statistical and ML models; DeepAR; Prophet; GBDT
Evaluation_Metrics: Model complexity; data requirements; computational scalability; bias stability
Key_Empirical_Findings: Establishes a rigorous taxonomy for industrial demand forecasting methods, proving that data pipeline integrity, temporal partitioning, and residual bias auditing outweigh algorithmic complexity.
Relevance_to_Our_Study: Informs our strict leakage-safe validation engine and automated tracking signal surveillance.

Authors: Fildes, Robert; Ma, Shaohui; Kolassa, Stephan
Title: Retail forecasting: Research and practice
Forecasting_Methods: Classical; ML; deep learning; promotional econometric models
Inventory_Setting: Retail supply chains; cross-docking; shelf allocation
Evaluation_Metrics: MAE; RMSE; WAPE; Fill Rate; Lost Sales
Key_Empirical_Findings: Reviews retail forecasting practices across academia and industry, emphasizing that retail series are dominated by promotional price shocks, extreme intermittency, and calendar clustering.
Relevance_to_Our_Study: Establishes the authoritative state of the art and benchmarks for retail demand forecasting across commercial channels.

Authors: Makridakis, Spyros; Spiliotis, Evangelos; Assimakopoulos, Vassilios
Title: M5 accuracy competition: Results, findings, and conclusions
Forecasting_Methods: LightGBM; XGBoost; CatBoost; Neural Networks; Classical statistical benchmarks
Evaluation_Metrics: WRMSSE; RMSSE; WAPE
Key_Empirical_Findings: Confirms across 42,840 series that gradient boosted decision trees decisively outperform classical statistical methods, with LightGBM dominating hierarchical retail sales forecasting.
Relevance_to_Our_Study: Provides the definitive empirical justification for gradient boosted decision tree ensembles on the M5 dataset.
